verdict.summary: You can connect your own account within minutes in Testing mode. Public use with read, modify or full-access Gmail scopes needs Google verification plus a CASA security assessment, which Google says can take several weeks. A sensitive-only scope set such as gmail.send avoids the assessment.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 days for the app and verification materials, plus assessment work for restricted scopes
verdict.approval_wait: 3-5 business days (sensitive scopes only); several weeks (restricted scopes, Google's wording; about 6 weeks per third-party sources)

gates.name: Testing mode / development
gates.unlocks: You and any users you list as test users can connect. No verification is needed while the app is in development or testing.
limits: A user cap and limited refresh-token lifetime apply in testing (Google). Third-party sources say 100 test users and a 7-day refresh token; neither figure is confirmed on Google's pages.
Test users see an unverified-app warning (third-party).
An Internal user type (Workspace only) limits the app to your own organization.

gates.name: Unverified app (100 new users) / sensitive-scope verification
gates.unlocks: Users outside your list can connect, up to 100 new users, behind the unverified-app screen. Sensitive-scope verification (for example gmail.send only) removes the warning and the cap.
limits: Unverified apps are capped at 100 new users in total. Google may adjust the cap per app.
The unverified-app screen shows while verification is pending or when scopes are not declared.
Workspace admins may block unverified or untrusted clients (admin_policy_enforced).
gates.time_to_reach: 3-5 business days for sensitive-scope verification, after brand verification

gates.name: Verified, with restricted-scope approval and CASA
gates.unlocks: Anyone can connect with restricted Gmail scopes (readonly, modify, compose, mail.google.com).
limits: A security assessment is required if you store or transmit restricted data on servers.
Reverification and reassessment are required at least every 12 months.
Adding scopes or changing the client later can force reverification.
Google may revoke tokens without notice if the app is no longer approved.
gates.time_to_reach: Several weeks (Google); about 6 weeks per third-party sources

steps.title: Decide: managed Composio auth or your own client
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Gmail app for prototyping. Register your own Google Cloud client if you need your own branding or a narrower scope set. The Composio defaults include mail.google.com, which is restricted.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and configure Google Auth Platform
steps.detail: Sign in at the Cloud Console, create a project, enable the Gmail API, and open Google Auth Platform / OAuth consent screen. Choose External (or Internal for a Workspace-only app) and fill in the app name, support email and contacts.
gotchas: Production apps used by 100 or more people need separate Cloud projects for testing and production.

steps.title: Choose the narrowest scopes and declare them
steps.detail: On the Data Access page, declare every scope you will use. Prefer gmail.send (sensitive) over gmail.readonly, gmail.modify or mail.google.com (restricted) wherever possible. Request mail.google.com only if you must permanently delete messages.

values.label: Scopes
values.value: Only the Gmail scopes your features need (for example https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send)

gotchas: Do not copy Composio's default scope list unchanged. It includes mail.google.com.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client (Web application)
steps.detail: Under Clients / Credentials, create an OAuth client of type Web application. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config as the authorized redirect URI. Copy the client ID and secret into the Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URIs must be HTTPS and match exactly, or you get a redirect URI mismatch.
Clients inactive for 6 months may be deleted.

steps.title: Add yourself as a test user and connect
steps.detail: Add your Google account and any testers as test users, then run an authorization through Composio. Expect the unverified-app warning and short-lived refresh tokens in Testing mode.

steps.title: Publish a home page and privacy policy
steps.detail: Draft a public home page that describes the app, plus a privacy policy on the same domain. The privacy policy must disclose how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared. For restricted scopes, include a Limited Use compliance statement. Link both from the consent screen.
gotchas: The home page must be public, not behind a login.
The in-app disclosure before consent cannot live only in the privacy policy.

steps.title: Verify domain ownership in Search Console
steps.detail: Verify your site in Search Console using an account that is a Project Owner or Editor on the OAuth project.

steps.title: Complete brand verification
steps.detail: Enter your branding info, click Verify Branding, then publish the branding. The automated check usually takes a few minutes.

steps.title: Request data-access verification
steps.detail: In the Verification Center, declare all scopes and give up to three documentation links. Justify each sensitive or restricted scope, and upload an unlisted YouTube demo video showing the OAuth flow and scope use.
gotchas: The app's use case must fit Google's allowed Gmail use cases. Mobile keyboards and one-time export are barred.
Limited Use data may not be used to train general AI/ML models.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment (restricted scopes only)
steps.detail: If you store or transmit restricted data on servers, complete the assessment with a Google-designated assessor. Encrypt user data and OAuth tokens at rest and use HTTPS. Skip this step if you use only sensitive scopes.
gotchas: Reassessment is needed at least every 12 months.

steps.title: Wait for Google's review
steps.detail: Sensitive-only verification typically takes 3-5 business days. Restricted verification can take several weeks. Respond to reviewer emails quickly.

steps.title: Publish to production and monitor
steps.detail: Set the publishing status to In production. Don't add scopes or change the client without planning for reverification. If you build a Gmail MCP agent, mark the client 'Use this client for an AI-powered agent' before 11 Nov 2026.

requirements.item: Public home page and privacy policy on a verified domain you own
requirements.detail: The home page must be public and relevant to the app. The privacy policy must be on the same domain and linked from the consent screen.
Done by a Project Owner or Editor. Google won't approve verification without it.

requirements.item: All scopes declared on the Data Access page
requirements.detail: Every scope you use must be declared there.
Provide an unlisted YouTube video and a justification for each sensitive or restricted scope.

requirements.item: CASA security assessment and annual reverification
requirements.detail: Needed for restricted scopes when data passes through your servers. Repeat at least every 12 months.

requirements.item: Permitted Gmail use case and Limited Use compliance
requirements.detail: The app must fit a Google-listed Gmail use case. Limited Use restrictions apply to AI/ML training and human reading of data.

requirements.item: Agentic client flag for Gmail MCP use
requirements.detail: From 11 Nov 2026, Workspace MCP servers reject OAuth clients not marked as agentic. Apps that only call REST APIs are unaffected.

scopes.effect: Needs sensitive-scope verification (3-5 business days). No CASA required if it is the only sensitive-tier scope set.
Needs restricted-scope verification and CASA for server-side storage.
Full access. Google says to request it only for permanent deletion. It is in Composio's defaults, so a BYO app copying them inherits restricted review.
Only for Workspace customers using a service account with domain-wide delegation.

blockers.symptom: Unverified app screen; sign-ups stop at 100 new users
blockers.cause: Sensitive or restricted scopes are in use without completed verification.
blockers.fix: Declare scopes, complete brand and data-access verification, and finish CASA if restricted.

blockers.cause: The user is not on the test user list while the app is in Testing.
blockers.fix: Add them as a test user or publish and verify the app.

blockers.cause: The URI registered in Google does not exactly match the one Composio sends.
blockers.fix: Copy the callback URL from your Composio auth config exactly. The Composio default redirect URI and the observed callback differ, so confirm which one Composio shows.

blockers.cause: Testing-mode refresh tokens expire (7 days per third-party sources). Tokens can also be revoked if the app loses approval.
blockers.fix: Move to production, or re-authorize the user.

blockers.cause: A Workspace admin restricts sensitive scopes for clients not marked trusted.
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to allowlist the OAuth client ID.

blockers.cause: Possible reasons: ownership not verified, missing privacy policy, or a disallowed use case.
blockers.fix: Complete Search Console verification, fix the policy pages, and align the use case with Google's listed Gmail uses.

composio.note: Start on managed auth for prototyping. Register your own Google Cloud client when you ship under your own branding or need narrower scopes. Composio's default scope set includes mail.google.com (restricted), so a BYO app that copies it would face restricted-scope verification and CASA (inferred). Confirm the exact redirect URI in your Composio auth config before registering it with Google.

open_questions: Google's refresh-token page was not fetched; the 7-day Testing expiry and 100-refresh-token cap come only from third-party sources.
The official Verification FAQ was not fetched; confirm gmail.readonly, gmail.modify and gmail.compose classifications there.
No official Google source gives a calendar time in weeks for restricted Gmail verification; six weeks is third-party.
No official source was found on Marketplace listing review or install minimums for Gmail apps.
The Composio default redirect URI differs from the callback seen in the authorize probe; confirm which one your Composio auth config shows.
CASA assessor cost and Letter of Assessment timing are unverified.
No official source for install caps on unreviewed apps beyond the 100-new-user cap.
Whether Gmail MCP developer-preview client rules change scope or verification for a BYO app was not determined.
